Pattern: a legitimate + N (business, claim)
Examples: The yard was a legitimate business for years. | He had a legitimate claim and no way to prove it.

Pattern: a premeditated + N (attack, crime)
Examples: The attack was clearly premeditated. | Nothing suggested a premeditated plan.

Pattern: suspicious + N (behaviour, circumstances)
Examples: Neighbours reported suspicious behaviour at the back gate. | The fire was treated as suspicious.

Pattern: be found/plead + guilty + of + N
Examples: He was found guilty on two counts. | She pleaded guilty and avoided a trial.

Pattern: be/prove sb + innocent
Examples: He spent nine years in prison though innocent. | Proving yourself innocent is nobody's job but your own.

Pattern: a convicted + N (fraudster, killer)
Examples: A convicted fraudster was running the charity. | Convicted drivers must retake the test.

Pattern: be wanted + for/in connection with + N
Examples: He is wanted in two countries. | She was wanted for questioning, not for arrest.

Pattern: a lenient + N (sentence, approach)
Examples: The sentence was criticised as lenient. | A lenient approach to first offences pays off later.

Pattern: a harsh + N (sentence, regime)
Examples: Harsh sentences filled the prisons and changed nothing. | The regime inside is harsher than the sentence implies.

Pattern: a law-abiding + N (citizen, family)
Examples: Law-abiding tenants were punished for their neighbours. | He describes himself as law-abiding and always has been.

Pattern: be under-reported; an under-reported + N
Examples: Domestic abuse remains badly under-reported. | Shoplifting is the most under-reported offence of all.

Pattern: an unsolved + N (case, crime)
Examples: The case has been unsolved for forty years. | Unsolved burglaries are quietly filed away.

Pattern: an armed + N (robbery, officer)
Examples: Armed officers were deployed for the first time here. | It was an armed robbery, though the gun was imitation.

Pattern: crack down on + N; không tách được
Examples: The council cracked down on unlicensed renting. | They cracked down on the trade and it moved online.

Pattern: get away with + N; không tách được
Examples: He got away with it for eleven years. | Nobody gets away with that twice.

Pattern: let off + sb hoặc let + sb + off; tách được
Examples: The magistrate let him off with a warning. | They let the youngest one off entirely.

Pattern: lock up + sb hoặc lock + sb + up; tách được
Examples: Locking up teenagers makes worse adults. | They locked him up for a fortnight on remand.

Pattern: break into + N; không tách được
Examples: Someone broke into the shed twice in a month. | They broke into the office and took nothing.

Pattern: make off with + N; không tách được
Examples: Thieves made off with the whole till. | He made off with two bicycles in daylight.

Pattern: look into + N; không tách được
Examples: Officers looked into the complaint and closed it. | The inspectorate is looking into both deaths.

Pattern: tip off + sb hoặc tip + sb + off; tách được
Examples: Someone tipped off the police that morning. | A neighbour tipped them off about the van.

Pattern: own up; own up to + N
Examples: He owned up to the damage the next day. | Nobody owned up and nobody was charged.

Pattern: hush up + N hoặc hush + N + up; tách được
Examples: The college tried to hush up both incidents. | They hushed the first case up completely.

Pattern: round up + N hoặc round + N + up; tách được
Examples: Officers rounded up nine suspects before dawn. | They rounded the crowd up at the junction.

Definition: đưa về để lấy lời khai
Pattern: bring in + sb hoặc bring + sb + in; tách được
Examples: Two men were brought in for questioning. | They brought him in at six in the morning.

Definition: ra đầu thú hoặc giao nộp
Pattern: turn + sb/oneself + in; tách được
Examples: He turned himself in a week later. | A relative turned him in for the reward.

Pattern: danh từ đếm được; a + crime hotspot + is identified
Examples: The junction was identified as a crime hotspot. | Two crime hotspots are a single street apart.

Definition: chính sách trị an không khoan nhượng
Pattern: danh từ không đếm được; adopt + zero-tolerance policing
Examples: Zero-tolerance policing filled the cells and emptied the trust. | The force adopted zero-tolerance policing for one summer.

Pattern: danh từ đếm được; a + prison officer + supervises
Examples: Prison officers are short-staffed on every wing. | One prison officer supervises forty men.

Pattern: danh từ đếm được; an + eyewitness + describes
Examples: Two eyewitnesses gave different descriptions. | Eyewitness accounts are weaker evidence than people assume.

Definition: tổ xử lí người chưa thành niên phạm tội
Pattern: danh từ đếm được; refer sb to + a youth offending team
Examples: He was referred to the youth offending team. | The youth offending team works with schools first.

Pattern: be/put oneself + above the law
Examples: The contractors behaved as if they were above the law. | Nobody in the licensing office is above the law.

Pattern: be/put sb + behind bars
Examples: He spent eleven years behind bars. | Putting more people behind bars solved nothing here.

Pattern: be caught + red-handed
Examples: They were caught red-handed with the cable. | He was caught red-handed and still denied it.

Pattern: get off + scot-free
Examples: The organisers got off scot-free. | Nobody expected him to get off scot-free.

Pattern: be/get + a slap on the wrist
Examples: The fine was a slap on the wrist. | They got a slap on the wrist and carried on.

Pattern: turn a blind eye + to + N
Examples: Inspectors turned a blind eye for years. | The licensing office turned a blind eye to the overcrowding.

Term: the long arm of the law
Pattern: the long arm of the law + reaches/catches up
Examples: The long arm of the law reached him in another country. | He trusted distance and the long arm of the law caught up.

Pattern: do time + for + N
Examples: He did time for handling stolen goods. | Doing time at nineteen shaped the rest of his life.

Pattern: come clean + about + N
Examples: He came clean about the second account. | She came clean only when the audit began.

Pattern: be/go + on the run
Examples: He was on the run for four months. | They went on the run and were found at a campsite.
